chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Abdul-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Jaludi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Zakariya told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Umara told us, from his father, saying:

I was present with Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon them both), and a man entered and asked him about 'Kaf-Ha-Ya-Ain-Sad'. So he, peace be upon him, said: 'Kaf' is Sufficient for our Shi'a; 'Ha' is a Guide for them; 'Ya' is a Protector for them; 'Ain' is Knowledgeable of the people of our obedience; 'Sad' is Truthful in His promise to them until He brings them to the rank He promised them in the depth of the Qur'an.

key_terms.الباقر: Al-Baqir, the fifth Imam, known for deep knowledge
key_terms.كَهيعص: The disjointed letters at the start of Surah Ta-Ha

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the letters Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad in Shia tafsir?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq elucidates the esoteric significance of the disjointed letters (Al-Huruf) in Surah Ta-Ha, interpreting them as a divine acronym for the attributes of the Ahl al-Bayt. This interpretation underscores the Shia belief in the spiritual authority and infallibility of the Imams, who serve as the ultimate guides and guarantors of the covenantal promises detailed in the Qur'an.
